segments.speaker: me
segments.text: This is the review of the brand refresh concepts from the studio. We have three directions.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Direction one keeps our current wordmark and updates the color palette to warmer tones.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Direction two is a new wordmark with a geometric typeface and a bolder accent color.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Direction three is the most radical: a new symbol that can work on its own as an app icon.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Let's talk about each. What did the customer panel prefer?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Direction two came out on top, especially with newer customers.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: Long-time customers preferred direction one, but not by much.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Direction three was polarizing, some loved it, some found it cold.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: What about accessibility of the color palettes?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: All three pass contrast checks for text, but direction two's accent color fails on white backgrounds for small text.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: The studio can darken it slightly.

segments.speaker: Speaker 4
segments.text: Direction one is the cheapest, it's mostly color tokens. Two and three need new assets everywhere.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: I'm leaning toward direction two with the darker accent.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Agreed. It feels like us, but more confident.

segments.speaker: Speaker 3
segments.text: I'd like to keep exploring the symbol from direction three as a secondary mark.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Let's ask the studio for a combined round. Two weeks?
